eligibility.quote: UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x80 in position 15: invalid start byte

failed_conditions.quote: There is a heavy mismatch here between the message/C++ types and Python types. `string` is 8-bit data which does not have encoding, neither does `std::string`. Message strings *ought* to be UTF-8, but this is not enforced. But Python strings always enforce an encoding. So it is perfectly possible to publish data from C++, which gets mangled when received in Python.

loudness.quote: UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x80 in position 15: invalid start byte

resolution.quote: With https://github.com/ros2/rosidl_python/pull/176 merged, I believe this issue is resolved for Rolling.

notes: Eligibility, class representation_convention (encoding of the string value crossing the boundary), and resolution recommended all agree with the sources I read. The loudness is WRONG: the spec claims loud_documented with detection_stage 'connect' and evidence 'the consumer logs an incompatibility error naming the element before any data is exchanged'. No such connection-time diagnostic exists. Both sides agree on std_msgs/String (the ROS 2 type hash matches, so the connection succeeds), and the failure is a runtime UnicodeDecodeError raised during message deserialization in the spin/take path (rclpy_take -> PyUnicode_DecodeUTF8 with 'strict'). That is a runtime crash, not a build/connect/activate tooling diagnostic; the correct classification is silent_documented with detection_stage 'run'. The strict-vs-replace decode fix (rosidl_python #176/#181) confirms the diagnostic is at data decode time, not connection time.
